> [!WARNING]
>
> **The MCPJam API is in preview.** It works today and w
e use it ourselves, but\n> it has not been generally announced and the surface may change, including in\n> breaking ways, while we
finish the design. Pin your integration to the\n> behaviors documented on this page, build a [tolerant\n> reader](#versioning--st
ability), and expect to revisit it. Feedback is very\n> welcome on [Discord](https://discord.gg/JEnDtz8X6z) or\n> [GitHub](https:/

/github.com/MCPJam/inspector/issues).

> [card] [Create an API key](https://app.mcpjam.com/settings/api-keys)
>
> Go straight
to key management in the hosted app. If you're signed out,\n> you'll be asked to sign in and then land right back on the API keys

page.

The MCPJam API lets you operate the MCP servers saved in your
[hosted](https://docs.mcpjam.com/hosted/overview.md) proje

cts (from CI, scripts, or your own agents)
without opening the UI.

What you can do with it today:

* **Discover your resourc

es**: list your projects, their servers, eval
 suites, and chat sessions, so every ID the other routes need is
 self-serve
*
**Validate a server**: connect, initialize, and capture a capability snapshot\n* **Run the doctor**: the probe → connect → initial
ize → capabilities workflow\n* **Check OAuth requirements**: does this server need an OAuth grant?\n* **List tools, prompts, and r
esources**: the server's MCP primitives\n* **Call a tool / render a prompt**: execute primitives and get the MCP result back verba

tim
* **Read a resource** by URI
* **Export a full snapshot**: tools, resources, and prompts as one JSON document
* **Manage a
project's clients**: list, read, **create** (from a built-in\n template like `claude`/`chatgpt`/`cursor`, or from a full config),
edit,\n duplicate, and delete the named, reusable configurations that define how\n MCPJam connects to and talks to your MCP ser
vers. Edits are compare-and-set:\n read the client, then send its `configId` back as `expectedConfigId` for a\n config change an
d its `name` back as `expectedName` for a rename (a rename\n does not rotate the config, so the config token cannot detect a conc
urrent\n one), and a concurrent edit is rejected rather than silently reverted\n* **Manage a project's environments**: list, read

, and archive the named
 execution bundles (host + optional server group) that eval
 suites and goals run against,
 and **pr
eview** what one resolves to before launching it\n* **List a project's studies**: name, access mode, attached servers, and\n shar
e link, and **read one study's settings**: model, system prompt,\n tool-approval policy, and resolved servers\n* **Author eval su
ites**: create a runnable suite (name, default model, servers, test cases) synchronously and get a `suiteId` back; no run is start
ed and no credits are spent\n* **Run eval suites asynchronously**: create a run from a saved suite, get a `202` + `runId`\n immed
iately, then poll status, per-iteration results (tool calls, token\n usage, latency), and full traces. Runs appear live in the ho

sted UI,
 tagged `source: "api"`
* **Manage a server's accounts**: complete OAuth yourself (e.g. the SDK's
 `runOAuthLogin`
, or your CI's own sign-in) and upload the token to a named\n account; list, rename, choose the default, and delete accounts. Tok

ens are
 write-only: no route returns one
* **Run a headless agent turn**: send a message history, get back the
 assistant re
ply, the platform operations it invoked, references to any\n resources it created (eval suites), and token usage; the model is pi

nned
 server-side and billed to the project
* **Send feedback**: report a bug, a missing capability, or something
 confusing

to the MCPJam team at the moment you hit it; the same endpoint the
 `send_feedback` MCP tool calls

All endpoints operate on s
ervers you have already added to a project in the\nhosted inspector. Managing API keys remains UI-only; see\n[Not in the API yet](

#not-in-the-api-yet).

## Base URL

```text theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1
```

The API

is path-versioned. All routes on this page are relative to the base
URL above.

## Authentication

Every request needs an MC

PJam API key in the `Authorization` header:

```bash theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
curl -X POST \
 "https://app.mcpja
m.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/servers/$SERVER_ID/tools\" \\\n -H \"Authorization: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KEY\" \\\n -H \"Content

-Type: application/json" \
 -d '{}'
```

### Creating a key

1. Open [**Settings → API keys**](https://app.mcpjam.com/set

tings/api-keys)
 in the hosted app (the card at the top of this page takes you there
 directly).
2. Click **Create API key*
*, name it, and pick the **organization** it will act in.\n3. Copy the key (`sk_…`) immediately; **it is shown exactly once** and

never
 stored by MCPJam in retrievable form.

Keys can be revoked from the same page at any time. Revocation takes effect
im

mediately.

### Scope

A key is bound to one MCPJam organization at creation and acts **as you,
inside that organization**. P
er-request authorization still applies: a call\nonly succeeds if the key's owner can access that project and server. A key\ncan ne

ver reach projects outside its organization.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Two deliberate restrictions while in preview:
>
> * **API keys c
annot manage API keys.** Requests to the key-management surface\n> with an `sk_…` bearer fail with `403 FORBIDDEN`. Create and r

evoke keys in
> the UI.
> * **Guest sessions cannot use the API.** Sign in to create keys.

### Keep keys secret

Treat an

API key like a password:

* Load it from an environment variable or secret manager; never commit it to
 source control or shi
p it in client-side code.\n* Scope keys narrowly: one key per integration, named so you can tell them apart.\n* Rotate by creating
a replacement key, switching traffic, then revoking the old one.\n* If a key leaks, revoke it immediately in\n [**Settings → API
keys**](https://app.mcpjam.com/settings/api-keys).\n\nIf you see `401 UNAUTHORIZED` with `details.reason: \"ORPHANED_KEY\"`, the
key\nis no longer bound to an organization and cannot be used; create a new key\nfrom [Settings](https://app.mcpjam.com/settings/a

pi-keys).

## Conventions

**Requests.** Operations on servers are `POST` with a JSON body (most accept
an empty `{}`). **Rea
ds**, the catalog listings and eval-run polling, are\n`GET` and take their options (`cursor`, `limit`, filters) as query\nparamete

rs.

**Responses.** Three envelope shapes, used consistently:

| Kind | Shape |
| - | - |
| Single resource | The resource o
bject directly |\n| Collection | `{ \"items\": [...], \"nextCursor\": \"...\" }`; `nextCursor` omitted on the last page |\n| Error
| `{ \"code\": \"...\", \"message\": \"...\", \"details\": {...} }` with a matching HTTP status |\n\n**Pagination.** Collections
are cursor-based. Pass the previous response's\n`nextCursor` as `cursor` in the next request (body field on `POST` lists,\nquery p
arameter on `GET` lists). Cursors are opaque; don't parse them.\n\n**Authoring vs running suites.** `POST /eval-suites` creates a
runnable suite\n(the suite plus its test cases) **synchronously** and responds `201` with the\n`suiteId`, WITHOUT running anything
; author once, run later. `POST /eval-runs`\nis the async counterpart: it validates and creates a run synchronously, then\ndetache
s execution and responds `202` with a `runId`. Poll\n`GET /eval-runs/{runId}` until `status` is `completed`, `failed`,\n`cancelled

`, or `timed_out`.

**IDs.** Every identifier the API takes is discoverable through the API
itself: `GET /projects` lists your
projects, `GET /projects/{projectId}/servers`\nlists each project's servers, and `GET /projects/{projectId}/eval-suites`\nlists it

s eval suites. Start from `GET /me` to confirm which account a key
acts as.

## Errors

Errors always use the canonical body
`{ code, message, details? }`. The `code`\nis stable and machine-readable; `message` is human-readable and may change;\n`details`

is an optional, unstructured bag.

| Code | HTTP | Meaning |
| - | - | - |
| `UNAUTHORIZED` | 401 | Missing, invalid, revoked,
or orphaned key |\n| `OAUTH_REQUIRED` | 401 | The **target MCP server** needs an OAuth grant; distinct from a bad key |\n| `AUTH_
